title: Separation of Judiciary from Executive
subject: Polity
caption: Organizational chart of the Judiciary as a separate entity from the Executive.
altText: A diagram illustrating the constitutional principle of separation of powers. The Constitution leads to the concept of Separation of Powers, which branches into Executive, Judiciary, and Legislative. The Executive branch includes the Prime Minister/President and Government Ministries. The Judiciary branch is shown as distinct, containing the Supreme Court, High Courts, Lower Courts, and functions such as Judicial Review and the Appointment Process, highlighting its independence from the Executive.
